name: Brainwashed Noble
summary: Deep in the caverns outside the Deadmines, Brainwashed Noble remains captive under Defias control. Magical manipulation has stripped him of his will, and he serves the Brotherhood alongside undead minions instead of walking Stormwind's grand halls.

sections.title: A Pawn of the Brotherhood
sections.body: Brainwashed Noble wanders the passages leading into the Deadmines, among bandits and rotting corpses. Remnants of highborn finery suggest he belonged to Stormwind's House of Nobles, perhaps as a sitting member or a scion. Edwin VanCleef took him captive, and the Defias chose enchantments over ransom, bending his mind into that of a spellcasting guard for their sanctuary. The Brotherhood's hatred of the peers who refused to pay after the city was rebuilt reaches even into the caverns beneath Westfall.

faq.answer: Brainwashed Noble is an aristocratic human presumed to come from Stormwind's House of Nobles. The Defias Brotherhood captured and magically subjugated him deep in the Deadmines caverns.

faq.q: Why is a Stormwind noble inside the Deadmines caves?
faq.answer: The Defias Brotherhood holds a bitter vendetta against Stormwind's aristocracy over debts left unpaid after the city was rebuilt. A captured noble gives them magical labor and a means of personal vengeance.

faq.q: Where can the Brainwashed Noble be found?
faq.answer: Brainwashed Noble can be found in the cavern tunnels of Moonbrook that lead toward the Deadmines entrance, among passages inhabited by skeletal undead.
The exact caster is unknown. Renegade spellcasters and enchanters among the Defias in Westfall are capable of bending a captive's mind through sorcery.

angles.text: As a human, seeing a peer of the realm reduced to a mindless sentry beneath Westfall shows the depth of the Defias Brotherhood's grudge against Stormwind's ruling elite.
As a mage, Brainwashed Noble uses magical staves and arcane tricks such as Polymorph, suggesting he had formal magical education in the capital before his mind was shattered.
